NOT JUDGED -- my test cannot measure this one, so treat its "failure" as meaningless.

Your solution uses CURVES: U curves on edges 0 and 3, opening a corner whose angle is forced to exactly 0 for every member of the family (3,000 sampled, none above 0.0000). The verifier develops the STRAIGHT polygon, which self-touches at that zero corner, so prepShape declares the tile invalid and overlapStrict returns its "not a tile at all" value. That is the straight-edge-proxy trap, not a verdict on your tiling.

You said "Now it's nice", and nothing I have measured contradicts that. Judging it properly means developing the CURVED boundary (TilerCurves.buildCurvedTiles) rather than the skeleton -- the same fix the reduce work needed. Until that is wired in, this row is unmeasured.

Worth remembering why it is interesting: a forced zero angle is NOT fatal when the flanking edges are curve-capable. This combo and #3234 m6 si8 both force a zero angle between U edges, and yours has a solution while #3234 does not.
